question: What is the IRS limit on employee elective deferrals to a 401(k) plan for 2027?
answer:
The IRS limit on employee elective deferrals to a 401(k) plan for 2027 is $25,500, up from $24,500 for 2026 (announced Nov. 12, 2026) [2][1]. The same limit applies to 403(b), governmental 457 plans, and the federal Thrift Savings Plan [2]. Employees aged 50 and over can generally contribute an additional $8,500 in catch-up contributions, for up to $34,000 a year [2]. For ages 60 through 63, the catch-up limit is $11,750 instead [2].

A draft IRS publication lists the older 2026 figure of $24,500, which is the prior-year limit and not the 2027 amount [4]. For decisions about your own contributions, it's worth talking with a qualified professional.

studyNotes.focus: The question asks for the 2027 IRS limit on employee elective deferrals (salary deferrals) to a 401(k) plan.

keyPoints.text: The 2027 limit on employee elective deferrals under section 402(g) for 401(k) plans is $25,500, up from $24,500 in 2026.
The IRS announced the 2027 401(k) deferral increase to $25,500 on November 12, 2026, via IR-2026-136 and Notice 2026-66.
Employees aged 50 and over can contribute a catch-up of $8,500 in 2027, for up to $34,000 total.
Employees aged 60 to 63 have a higher 2027 catch-up limit of $11,750 under SECURE 2.0.
The same $25,500 limit applies to 403(b), governmental 457 plans, and the federal Thrift Savings Plan.
